csharp.bcl.description: C# / .NET base class library -> C++ and Java. The 'cpp' rows are demonstrator rows; the 'java' rows are the rebinding the C# kit makes on the way to the C++03 back end, whose runtime is Java's library (codebreaker/translate/dotnet/cs2cpp.py): one row per BCL call it carries, 'unsupported' where it refuses with the reason.

glu.description: OpenGL Utility (GLU) -> Direct3D 9 for Xbox 360. Matrix builders map to D3DX; texture build maps to the D3D9 texture helper; picking maps to the D3D9 software-pick helper. No OpenGL at runtime.

java.csharp.description: Java's library -> C# / .NET, as the C# back end writes it (codebreaker/translate/backends/csharp_java.py). A key is Family.method/arity, or Family.method(firstParamType) where overloads differ by type; a family is a group of Java classes that answer the same way (List: List, ArrayList, LinkedList, Collection, ...). A target is a template: {t} the receiver, {0} {1} .. the arguments, {0p} an argument as an operand, {*} every argument, {s0} an argument as Java turns it into text (JavaRt.Str where .NET's text differs). 'kind' says how close: direct (the same meaning), signature-adapted (the same meaning through a different call), shim (JavaRt, the Java runtime in C#), unsupported (no faithful form: the method is declined). A 'stmt' target is used where the call is a statement and its value unused.

java.lang.description: java.lang core: math, strings, boxing, System. Targets are C++; a few rows carry by_version overrides to demonstrate the dialect axis (e.g. the null literal and the type-generic <cmath> overloads landed in C++11).

java.nio.description: Java NIO buffers. On Xbox 360 these resolve to the hand-written NIOBuffers platform layer (a typed view over a heap allocation); the rows below are the contract that layer must satisfy.

java.util.description: java.util collections -> the converter's J-container runtime (JList/JMap/JSet over std containers).

javax.swing.description: AWT/Swing desktop UI. Almost entirely dead on console; the few reachable calls resolve to a minimal shim (or an on-screen-keyboard / log) so they compile.

libc.description: C's standard library -> Java: what the Java back end (codebreaker/translate/backends/java.py) calls for each C library function. 'shim' rows are crt.LibC (codebreaker/translate/backends/java_runtime/crt/LibC.java), statically imported; 'direct' rows are the JDK's own; 'unsupported' rows are refused with the note.

lwjgl.input.description: LWJGL Keyboard/Mouse/Display. On Xbox 360 the controller adapter synthesizes key/mouse events; key CONSTANTS must all resolve so bind tables compile.

opengl.description: The OpenGL 1.x (LWJGL GL11) -> Direct3D 9 for Xbox 360 CONVERSION TABLE. The 360 does NOT run OpenGL; every call is converted to native Direct3D 9. 'kind': direct = a 1:1 IDirect3DDevice9/D3DX call; constant = a D3D enum; d3d9-helper = one of the three STATEFUL GL concepts that has no single D3D9 call (immediate mode, matrix stack, display lists) and is realized by a small Direct3D 9 helper (named in 'target'). No runtime OpenGL anywhere.

python.builtins.description: CPython builtins / stdlib -> C++ and C. The cpp targets (C++17 forms) are what the Python front end (codebreaker/translate/frontends/python) writes through backends/cpp17.py: a target is a template ({recv} the receiver, {0}.. the arguments, {args} all of them, {T} the result type) over native/ported/include/py.hpp.
